key_provisions.after: Enrolled act created a qualified data center sales tax exemption for construction, equipment, eligible costs and certain labor, subject to a $250 million investment commitment, jobs and other conditions; eligible costs exclude electricity. It also limits a specified economic-development electric-rate discount and requires fusion-center review and approval before public financial assistance or benefits. K.S.A. 74-50,333(a) and Revenue Notice 25-03 apply the exemption to qualified purchases made on or after July 1, 2025; approval still requires Commerce certification.

key_provisions.after: Expands Clean Energy Transformation Act coverage to certain port districts, single-customer consumer-owned utilities, and affected market customers; committee reports describe the bill as closing data center clean-power compliance gaps. The codified consumer-owned utility definition excludes a public utility district formed under Title 54 RCW with only one retail electric customer in Washington, provided that customer remains the same as of January 1, 2026 and the district continues receiving 100 percent of its electricity needs from Bonneville Power Administration.

proposed_fields.status: Governor-signed order dated August 6, 2026; official journal lists the padded number 2026-0494 as filed August 6, 2026, and the filed copy includes the attestation/seal and received-and-filed stamp. The order expressly states effectiveness August 6, 2026; subsequent legal force remains unverified.
proposed_fields.key_provisions: Requires data-center developers to submit energy plans protecting residential ratepayers and assuring energy needs can be met now, in the near term and long term without additional costs to other utility ratepayers. Directs the Public Service Commission not to allow utilities to increase rates paid by other ratepayers to recover costs caused by data-center development and operation. Directs the Energy and Environment Cabinet to deny permit applications where a data center would negatively affect listed environmental resources and requires compliance with applicable environmental laws and public-engagement requirements. Requires tax and community-engagement commitments and preserves local-community decisions on data-center operations. The order does not establish a categorical moratorium or repeal all statutory incentives.
proposed_fields.end_condition: No express end date identified in the complete two-page order. Later amendment, rescission, judicial developments and actual project applicability remain unverified.
